slides.text: In 1920, the farmers of Kandel, a small village in Dhamtari, about 70 km from Raipur, performed a water canal Satyagraha against the decree of irrigation tax imposed by the British rule. Due to which Mahatma Gandhi was well impressed and joined the peasant movement in Dhamtari on 21 December 1920 to support the farmers. Due to which the British were sweated, all the Gudhaan property which was confiscated by the British got it returned.

slides.text: The Kandel Canal Satyagraha proved to be a very effective step against the British. On his return, Gandhi addressed a public meeting in Raipur. The place where Gandhi gave a speech is today known as Gandhi Chowk in Raipur.

slides.text: Mahatma Gandhi's first visit to Chhattisgarh was in December 1920. Although not mentioned in Gandhi's history, there is enough information from various local sources that Mahatma Gandhi came to Raipur in connection with the Kandel Canal Satyagraha and went to Dhamtari, Kurud. Bal G angadhar Tilak, who was conferred with the title of Lokmanya, the most popular leader of that era, died on 1 August 1920.

slides.text: Meanwhile, in the Kandel village of Dhamtari district, the Satyagraha of the farmers was going on under the leadership of Babu Chhotelal Srivastava. Narayanrao Meghawale w as also supporting the S atyagraha. The government's irrigation department accused the farmers of Kandel of stealing water from the canal.

slides.text: Gandhi was accompanied by prominent leaders of the Khilafat Movement Shaukat Ali and his brother Muhammad Ali and mother of the Ali brothers. In the evening, Mahatma Gandhi addressed a huge general meeting. That place is famous today as Gandhi Chowk in Raipur.

slides.text: On 21 December 1920, Gandhi left Abbas B hai's motor to Dhamtari in front of the Balasamaj library located at Azad Chowk. On receiving the information about Gandhi's arrival, the irrigation officials swelled hands and withdrew the anti-farmer order. Returning from Dhamtari, Mahatma Gandhi addressed a massive public meeting in the ground next to the Anand S amaja library in Kankalipara.
